## Captured excerpt

This control outlines the practice of designing AI systems — particularly LLM and RAG systems that produce informational content — to provide verifiable citations, references, or traceable links back to the original source data or knowledge used to formulate their outputs.

Key ideas captured from the source include:
- verifiability requires a clear path back to source material
- transparency of sourcing matters
- attribution should be accurate and granular enough to be useful
- metadata preservation is important
- RAG pipelines need robust chunk-to-output linkage
- systems should handle uncitable or highly abstractive content honestly
- link rot, versioning, and source persistence are real implementation concerns
- citation presence does not by itself guarantee source quality
